newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet board to meet July 9 - sources.
newsitem.headline: Eramet board to meet July 9 - sources.

text.p: The board meeting of French mining group Eramet, delayed from June 24, will take place on July 9, industry sources said on Thursday.

The board meeting had been postponed to give the new Socialist government more time to review issues linked to a bitter dispute between Eramet and the previous conservative government over mining rights in New Caledonia.
Board members meeting on July 9 are expected to set a date for the annual general meeting, sources said. Eramet had no comment.
Eramet had cancelled the AGM due on May 29 amid deteriorating relations with its main shareholder, state holding Erap.
Erap, which owns 55 percent of Eramet, has threatened to take control of the board and oust chairman Yves Rambaud, who opposes any plans to limit the group's expansion in New Caledonia.

The previous government supported a plan by local Kanak company Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) to build a nickel smelter in the north of the French territory with Canadian group Falconbrige, using nickel from one of Eramet's mines.
The move was to appease local Kanak separatists ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence.

Beside Erap's proposal to oust Rambaud, board members were to have reviewed on June 24 proposals by minority shareholders aimed at insuring the independence of the future board. The Socialist government has not yet disclosed its intentions on the politically-sensitive issue of the New Caledonia smelter nor on the future of Rambaud.
